## The three tiers

- **AI-native specialists** — LlamaParse, Reducto, Landing AI ADE, Mistral Document AI. Leading on benchmarks, flexible pricing, less procurement maturity.
- **Hyperscaler APIs** — Google Document AI, AWS Textract, Azure Document Intelligence. Mature, broad-compliance-ready, architecturally template-leaning, lagging the agentic frontier on tables.
- **Classic IDP retrofitted** — ABBYY, Hyperscience, UiPath, Klippa, Rossum, Docsumo, Nanonets. Strong HITL, strong compliance, weak agentic story (with exceptions).
- **The new fourth tier** — platform-integrated agentic OCR (Databricks Document Intelligence). Not a pure-play vendor but increasingly relevant for enterprises already on those platforms.

## AI-native specialists

### LlamaParse (LlamaIndex)

- Four tiers: Fast (1 credit/page), Cost-Effective (3), Agentic (10), Agentic Plus (45). 1,000 credits = $1.25. 10k free credits/month.
- Effective per-page: $0.00125 → $0.05625.
- Top of ParseBench: **LlamaParse Agentic at 84.9% overall, ~$0.012/page.**
- Strong on: messy enterprise documents, financial filings, scientific papers.
- Caveat: vendor-published benchmark; expect rule-selection bias.

### Reducto

- Hybrid CV + VLM architecture. Multi-pass agentic OCR explicitly marketed.
- Top of RD-TableBench (their own benchmark) at ~0.90 similarity. ~20pp ahead of hyperscalers on tables.
- Strong on: complex tables, scanned PDFs, handwritten content.
- Caveat: RD-TableBench is vendor-published. Cross-validate on independent benchmarks.

### Landing AI — Agentic Document Extraction (ADE)

- Credit-based monthly subscriptions: $39/mo for 120k credits → $2,199/mo for 900k pages.
- Credit formula: `credits = ceil((input_chars/5000) + (output_chars/1000), 0.1)`.
- HIPAA + ZDR (Zero Data Retention) on Team/Enterprise plans.
- Strong on: regulated industries, structured ontology coverage (IDs, barcodes, attestations).
- New features (2025–2026): agentic table captioning, RBAC, expanded chunk ontology.

### Mistral Document AI (OCR 3)

- Model id `mistral-ocr-2512`. **$2 per 1,000 pages standard; $1 per 1,000 pages via Batch API.**
- Throughput: 2,000 pages/min per node.
- Self-host option — relevant for HIPAA and EU data-sovereignty workloads.
- Strong on: cost; speed; forms and handwriting (74% win rate vs. OCR 2).
- The price floor for "agentic-grade" parsing in 2026.

## Hyperscaler APIs

### Google Document AI

- Form Parser, Custom Document Classifier, etc. Mature; template-leaning.
- Per-page: $0.015–$0.065 depending on processor.
- Strong on: integration with GCP, broad compliance.
- Weak on: agentic loop, tables vs. specialists.

### AWS Textract

- Per-page: $0.0015 (basic) to $0.065 (Queries/AnalyzeDocument).
- Strong on: scale, A2I integration for HITL.
- Weak on: agentic feature set, tables vs. Reducto.

### Azure Document Intelligence

- Per-page: $0.0015–$0.050. Custom models supported.
- Strong on: custom models for narrow domains; Microsoft integration.
- Weak on: agentic positioning; OOTB workflows.

## Classic IDP, retrofitted

### ABBYY Vantage, Hyperscience, UiPath, Klippa, Rossum

- Strong compliance posture (SOC2/HIPAA/GDPR).
- HITL is native, not bolted on.
- Per-page: $0.020–$0.150 (Hyperscience at the high end).
- Weak on: agentic story is largely retrofitted. The model layer is being upgraded; the surrounding architecture is older.

### Nanonets and Docsumo (newer "AI-native commercial IDP")

- **Nanonets:** workflow-block pricing ($0.30/complex AI block, <$2/invoice end-to-end), 100+ languages, claims 34% of Fortune 500.
- **Docsumo:** 150+ document types, claims 95%+ accuracy. Tiered subscriptions; aggressive on agentic positioning in marketing.
- Both are stronger on agentic features than ABBYY-tier IDP, weaker on raw benchmark scores than AI-native specialists.

## Databricks Document Intelligence (the platform tier)

- `ai_parse_document` (GA), `ai_classify`, `ai_extract` as chainable AI functions.
- Tightly integrated with Lakeflow, Unity Catalog, Agent Bricks.
- Claims: **5–7× cheaper than VLM-only pipelines** for equivalent accuracy; one customer (Loopback Analytics) reports ~90% cost reduction on clinical-note extraction.
- The strategic significance: a data platform vendor saying out loud that **document reading is the gating constraint on agent quality**. That's air cover for the shift-left thesis.

## How to read this landscape

- Benchmark rank is not procurement rank. The vendors winning the leaderboards are often the youngest, with the thinnest enterprise-readiness story.
- The right question is "which vendor minimizes my cost-per-correct-extraction-with-provenance," not "which vendor scored highest on ParseBench."
- Procurement tip: shortlist three vendors across the three tiers (one AI-native, one hyperscaler, one classic IDP). Run all three on your golden set. Decide on data, not demos.

## Named takes

> *"The hyperscaler APIs are still where most enterprise procurement lands, and they are still the wrong choice for 2026 agentic workloads. They were designed for templates."*

> *"Pricing differences across vendors look big until you remember that error rate is the multiplier. A 4× cheaper parser with a 4× higher field-error rate is the same cost-per-correct-extraction."*
